newsitem.title: USA: NYS Senate OKs bill to ease merger of localities.
newsitem.headline: NYS Senate OKs bill to ease merger of localities.

text.p: The New York State Senate on Monday said it approved a measure that would make it easier for local governments to merge, saying this would help them provide services more efficiently at a lower cost.
"Local property taxes could be significantly reduced by consolidating local governments and services," said Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, in prepared remarks.
He noted that consolidation plans were being weighed in Schenectady and Buffalo, and the Town of Highlands and Village of Highland Falls, in Orange County.

The bill, which also must be approved by the Assembly and Gov George Pataki, would set the specific steps local governments would be required to take in order to consolidate functions or public offices.
Such a merger would have to be preceded by:
--a joint hearing held by the governing boards of the merging entities.
--a referendum held 90 days after the hearing, in which a majority of the voters would have to approve the plan.
